title: Adding a catalog tool above the mounted machine's max rpm says nothing until verify holds the post (EM-0300-2FL 15000 rpm on a 10000 rpm 770MX)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

body:
Found by the reporter in v0.26.0 via the AI Chat panel (2026-11-23). Reproduced headlessly with the 0.26.0 `camcraft-cli`; the same code is on `main`.

## What happens

On a mounted Tormach 770MX (ML) (`spindle_max` 10000 rpm), `add_tool { "catalog": "EM-0300-2FL" }` and `add_tool { "catalog": "EM-0400-2FL" }` copy the catalog's 15000 and 12000 rpm into the document as they are. Nothing says they are above the machine: the `add_tool` reply carries only the holder note, `add_operation` and `generate` add no note, and the first word of it is the machine check at verify / post, which holds the program:

```
machine Tormach 770MX (ML): 2 limit problem(s): 2D Adaptive1: tool EM-0300-2FL runs 15000 rpm, above the machine's 10000; 2D Contour1: tool EM-0400-2FL runs 12000 rpm, above the machine's 10000
```

The block itself is right (the Prime Directive holds: no over-limit S word is posted). The defect is that it comes last, after the work is generated, and that the other paths that set a speed already hold it to the machine and say so:

- `apply_cutting_data` / `suggest_cutting_data` (`crates/app/src/cutting.rs`, `compute`): "45094 rpm held to the machine's 10000".
- the Feeds tab spindle row (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/spindle_row.rs`, `hold_to_machine`): "spindle speed N rpm held to the machine's maximum M".

Only adding a catalog tool (MCP `add_tool`, `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs` `add_tool` -> `AddTool::with_holder`) takes the catalog rpm with no reading of the mounted machine. The verify problem also does not say what to do about it (edit the tool's speed, or `apply_cutting_data`).

## Steps to reproduce

`simple.step` is a 25.4 x 25.4 x 1.27 mm plate. Script `b.js`, run with `camcraft-cli script b.js`:

```js
cam.import("simple.step", "simple");
cam.call("load_machine", {builtin: "Tormach 770MX (ML)"});
cam.call("set_stock", {box: {dx: 37.4, dy: 37.4, dz: 5.27}});
cam.log(JSON.stringify(cam.call("add_tool", {catalog: "EM-0300-2FL"})));   // no rpm word
cam.log(JSON.stringify(cam.call("add_tool", {catalog: "EM-0400-2FL"})));   // no rpm word
cam.call("add_operation", {kind: "2D Adaptive", tool: "EM-0300-2FL", source: "stock"});
cam.call("add_operation", {kind: "2D Contour", tool: "EM-0400-2FL", source: "simple"});
cam.generate();                       // generates, no rpm note
cam.log(JSON.stringify(cam.verify())); // gate ok:false, the problem above
```

## Expected

When a tool is added (MCP `add_tool`, and the UI's add from the catalog) while a machine with a `spindle_max` (or `spindle_min`) is mounted and the tool's rpm is outside it, the reply / status says so at once, e.g. `"warning": "EM-0300-2FL runs 15000 rpm, above the Tormach 770MX (ML)'s 10000 - the post will be held; set the tool's speed (edit_tool) or apply_cutting_data"`. The machine check at verify keeps blocking as now, and its problem line names the same fix. The tool's rpm is not changed silently by the add (a library speed stays what the user stated; the warning tells them).

## Where

- `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs` `add_tool` (the reply has `note` for the holder only).
- `crates/app/src/commands/tool.rs` `AddTool` (where a note like the holder note can be built from the mounted machine).
- `crates/post/src/machine/check.rs` and `crates/app/src/posting_default_machine.rs`: the "runs N rpm, above the machine's M" problem text, which could name the fix.
- For comparison: `crates/app/src/cutting.rs` (`compute`, the clamp with a note) and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/spindle_row.rs` (`hold_to_machine`).

Related: #3457 (the lathe sibling: catalog TN-1600-0R8's 3000 rpm over the Tormach 15L's 2500, a first post held).

Priority P7 (a late refusal that could say more and an owed warning; the block is correct and the workaround is plain: edit the speed or apply cutting data). Effort medium: a note in one command's reply and the UI add path, plus the problem wording, with a test; posted G-code, the machine check and the gate do not change (if the fix instead clamps the rpm at add, it changes posted S words and is effort:high by the safety floor).

Done means: with the Tormach 770MX (ML) mounted, `add_tool { "catalog": "EM-0300-2FL" }` returns a warning naming 15000 rpm and the machine's 10000, the UI's catalog add shows the same text, a tool within the range gets no warning, and verify still blocks the post with a problem line that names the fix; pinned by a test in `crates/app/tests/`.
